newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: Costa Rica tax plan goes to Congress Jan 23.
newsitem.headline: Costa Rica tax plan goes to Congress Jan 23.

text.p: Costa Rican president Jose Maria Figueres said his government would start sending to Congress from January 23 its ambititious proposed privatization and tax reform program.
Figueres told a news conference that a group of lawyers would also revise the initiatives to check drafts and fit them with current legislation.
Tax reform proposals would be submitted first when Congress restarted sessions January 23, followed later by privatisation legislation which was still being worked on, he added.

Figueres first announced his program December 16. It includes the sale of two banks, the government communications company RACSA, part of the state insurance company and other assets, to help pay off crippling internal debts estimated at around $3.5 billion.
Private sector leaders have called for an overall privatization law to set a clear legal framework for the individual sales.
However, given that 1997 is an election year in Costa Rica, analysts say it is not clear how much of the initiative will pass Congress.
